newsitem.title: USA: Honeywell buying Measurex for $600 million.
newsitem.headline: Honeywell buying Measurex for $600 million.

text.p: Honeywell Inc., a global manufacturer of control systems for home and industry, will acquire Measurex Corp. for $600 million in cash, the companies said Monday.

The transaction is expected to strengthen Honeywell's position as a supplier of systems, services and products for the worldwide pulp and paper manufacturing industry, the companies said in a joint statement.
Under the terms of the agreement, which was approved by the boards of directors of both companies, Honeywell agreed to buy all of the outstanding shares of Measurex for $35 a share.
Measurex stock closed Friday at $24.50 on the New York Stock Exchange and its opening was delayed Monday. Honeywell traded early Monday at $70.125, up 12.5 cents a share, also on the NYES.
The companies acknowledged "that a rationalisation of redundant functions will occur," but did not specify how many people might lose their jobs.
"Today's announcement signals a major step that will broaden Honeywell's base in the important pulp and paper industry," said Michael Bonsignore, chairman of Honeywell.

"We see this transaction as a way to unite the particular strengths of each of our companies," said David Bossen, chairman of Measurex. "In this way, we'll be able to deliver a complete suite of automation solutions for pulp and paper manufacturers, extending from the woodyard to the shipping dock."

Honeywell provides industrial automation and control, including process control applications for the pulping industry, and a broad range of instrumentation. Measurex is a large provider of paper machine integrated control systems.
The merger should provide opportunities for stronger growth for Honeywell in the pulp and paper industry as well as reductions in costs, Bonsignore said.

The business unit will be run within Honeywell Industrial Automation and Control by John Gingerich, who has been president of Measurex. He will report to Markos Tambakeras, president of Honeywell Industrial Control.
Honeywell employs 53,000 people in 95 countries, with 1996 sales of $7.3 billion. Measurex has offices in 34 countries and had 1996 sales of $287 million.
